question: Does >70% asymmetric 3-px overlap vs the r13-lattice-s5 registry raster prove lane drift (PR #22 audit, AUDIT_REVIEW_2026-10-27.md finding 1)?
conclusion: The literal any-raster reading fails every raster ever scored in the fleet, including the 0.2778 champion and uniform-random dot sets, because the calibration lattice covers 99.87% of the footprint by design. It therefore cannot discriminate lane drift. The shared template validator (scripts/validate_submission.py Gate 3) implements the pre-documented null-calibrated/harmonic interpretation (IR-REG-LATTICE-03); rerun 2026-10-27 it passes the promoted file 5/5. Harmonic overlap vs the lattice is 22.6% and max vs competing detectors is 64.91%, both <=70%.
policy_note_for_selector: If the owner instead adopts the literal any-registry-raster reading, then no candidate from any site can ever be promoted while the lattice remains in the registry; that policy choice belongs to the selector step (Protocol Rule 6), and is stated explicitly in EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md so the decision is visible, not buried.
